hypothesis: Search one capacity corridor per physical interface/layer while wire order remains symbolic, then recover identities and concrete slots collectively. Avoid geometric-slot branching and tiny-hypergraph optimization for certified allocations.
mechanism: Capacity-edge A* with exact residual capacity in the existing discrete slot pool, followed by parity classes for pairwise interface orders, synchronized constraints across cells, total-order realization and independent zero-crossing/identity checks. Accepted allocations return before DuplicateCongestedPortSolver and Tiny search/section optimization. This is an upstream state-space quotient, not a uniform-port postprocessor.
domain: Complete greedy corridor allocation for ordinary routes whose selected terminal layers agree. Existing occupancy, preloaded sections/fixed-net ports, off-board interfaces, differentialPairs and buses are explicitly unsupported. Boundary-only nodes admit order constraints; interfaces touching interior terminals are locked. No via-placement or coupled timing allocator is implemented.
incompleteness: A greedy corridor path choice may exhaust capacity although another allocation exists. An unanchored parity orientation can fail total-order realization although another orientation works. Such failures reject only this compiler candidate and dispatch unchanged native routing; they never certify global infeasibility.
quality_evidence: Initial experiment accepted the existing differential-pair fixture topologically but produced 2.82mm final skew against its 0.05mm requirement. This exposed the missing bundle/timing state. Differential-pair and bus inputs now take an explicit unsupported-domain dispatch before compilation. Existing pad-clearance/length-match regression passes with this guard; budgets and constraints are unchanged.
positive_fixture: Unmodified fixtures/legacy/assets/e2e4.json: 132 serialized ports, 44 capacity edges, 29 corridor relaxations, 63 residual slot arcs not expanded, 2 complete routes and 6 allocated crossings. No shared multiwire groups occur there; the separate three-interface construction and exhaustive three-wire permutation oracle validate symbolic propagation.
physical_validation: The existing fixture completes P9, preserves all requested endpoints and has no independent copper DRC errors. Legacy fixture endpoint metadata is absent, so connectivity-checker findings are required to coincide with requested endpoints; internal dangling endpoints are rejected. Physical HD/obstacle/width/DRC stages remain unchanged.
timing: Compilation occurs in the port-pathing constructor, outside the existing P9 phase timer. Numeric symbolicCorridorCompileTimeMs and replay setup time expose that cost. End-to-end paired Blacksmith elapsed is primary; port-pathing phase timing alone must not be reported as a speedup.
work_removed: On accepted problems, no duplicate-port solve or Tiny search runs. Phase stats report residual edge relaxations, heap pops, unexpanded slot arcs, allocated crossings, order variables/equations, conflicts and skipped native calls. Counters are work evidence, not an estimate of baseline CPU savings.
validation: Exhaustive 36 left/right boundary-order cases against all 36 two-interface permutations
Three-interface capacity compression and concrete identity continuity
Constructor acceptance with terminal pcb_port_id preservation and computeNodePfMap
Differential pair and bus domain guards
Existing Tiny lazy-stats, terminal-id and error-propagation regressions
falsifiers: Accepted coverage or useful slot multiplicity is too small
Compiler setup/rejection work exceeds removed native search
A strict full-board quality regression remains
Even with meaningful shared-lane activation, end-to-end paired speedup is far below 10x
performance_claim: None before paired Blacksmith results. Negative results apply to this bounded strand compiler, not to a complete symbolic embedding, via-order or timing-aware bundle router.
